meta.methodology: Read framework.md, torah_70_packages.json, all reference===70 edges from torahData.js, and the full source text torah_70.txt. For each bechina statement in the source text, verified whether the concept appears as a node in the dataset and whether it is assigned to a package. Only concepts with explicit bechina language (בְּחִינַת, הַיְנוּ בְּחִינַת, נִקְרָא, לְשׁוֹן) were considered. The four eitza edges (814, 1423, 1980, 2415) were examined to determine whether their classification as eitza is accurate or whether some should be reclassified as bechina.

additions.reason: Line 6 of the source text states: 'הוּא יְסוֹד עוֹלָם, הַיְנוּ בְּחִינַת עָפָר' — 'he is the foundation of the world, meaning a bechina of dust.' The word הַיְנוּ is the Rebbe's standard bechina-declaration marker. יסוד עולם is an explicit aspect/bechina of עפר in this Torah. It belongs in Package 1 alongside עפר. The verse cited is 'וְצַדִּיק יְסוֹד עוֹלָם' (Proverbs 10:25) — the righteous person IS the world's foundation, and that foundation-quality IS dust/earthness. The concept יסוד עולם names the structural role of the tzaddik and is bechina-equivalent to both עפר and צדיק in this Torah.
additions.source_quote: הוּא יְסוֹד עוֹלָם, הַיְנוּ בְּחִינַת עָפָר, שֶׁכָּל הַדְּבָרִים הֵם עָלָיו כַּנַּ"ל

additions.reason: Line 13 of the source text states: 'אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהָקִים אֶת הַמִּשְׁכָּן, אֶלָּא הַצַּדִּיק שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת עָפָר, בְּחִינַת מֹשֶׁה' — only the tzaddik who is a bechina of dust, a bechina of Moshe, can erect the Mishkan. The double use of בְּחִינַת establishes a three-way equation: the tzaddik = bechina of dust = bechina of Moshe. Moshe is the archetypal tzaddik in this Torah — 'the most humble of all people' (Numbers 12:3) is the proof that he is the prime instance of the dust-quality. He belongs in Package 1 as the named human exemplar of the bechina-chain's entire logic. Moshe also directly connects to the Mishkan (he erected it, Exodus 40:18), completing the circle: Moshe = dust = drawing force = Mishkan.
additions.source_quote: אֶלָּא הַצַּדִּיק שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת עָפָר, בְּחִינַת מֹשֶׁה, שֶׁהָיָה עָנָו מִכָּל הָאָדָם

additions.reason: Line 14 of the source text quotes Isaiah 57:15: 'אֶשְׁכֹּן אֶת דַּכָּא' and introduces it explicitly as a bechina: 'וְזֶה בְּחִינַת (ישעיהו נ"ז): אֶשְׁכֹּן אֶת דַּכָּא'. The Rebbe then explains: through lowliness (שפלות), through making oneself like dust (כעפר), one acquires the drawing force (כח המושך) — and THIS is the bechina of the Mishkan. דַּכָּא (the crushed/lowly one, from the Isaiah verse) is therefore a bechina of the entire cluster: it is the biblical name for the quality of dust-humility that draws the Shechina. It belongs in Package 1 as the prophetic expression of the same essential nature.
additions.source_quote: וְזֶה בְּחִינַת (יְשַׁעְיָה נ"ז:ט"ו): אֶשְׁכֹּן אֶת דַּכָּא, כִּי עַל־יְדֵי שִׁפְלוּת, שֶׁמֵּשִׂים עַצְמוֹ כְּעָפָר, עַל־יְדֵי־זֶה יֵשׁ לוֹ כֹּחַ הַמּוֹשֵׁךְ

additions.reason: Line 15 of the source text states: 'וְזֶה בְּחִינַת הַכָּבוֹד הַנֶּאֱמַר אֵצֶל הַמִּשְׁכָּן' — 'This is the bechina of the honor/glory that is said regarding the Mishkan.' The verse cited is 'וּכְבוֹד ה' מָלֵא אֶת הַמִּשְׁכָּן' (Exodus 40:34). The Rebbe establishes that כָּבוֹד (divine honor/glory) is a bechina of the Mishkan — all human honor flows from this tzaddik who is a bechina of dust and Mishkan. This is not a description of an outcome (eitza) but a parallel essence: the Mishkan IS the dwelling-place of honor, honor IS the nature of the Mishkan. The Talmudic principle quoted — 'wherever you find His greatness, there you find His humility' (Megilla 31a) — confirms that the same essential nature (lowliness/dust) is simultaneously the location of all honor (כבוד). כבוד belongs in Package 1.
additions.source_quote: וְזֶה בְּחִינַת הַכָּבוֹד הַנֶּאֱמַר אֵצֶל הַמִּשְׁכָּן... כִּי כָּל הַכָּבוֹד שֶׁיֵּשׁ לְכָל אָדָם שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם, מִקָּטֹן וְעַד גָּדוֹל, כֻּלָּם הֵם מְקַבְּלִים רַק מִזֶּה הַצַּדִּיק, שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת עָפָר, בְּחִינַת מִשְׁכָּן

additions.reason: Line 12 of the source text states: 'הַמִּשְׁכָּן הוּא לְשׁוֹן מַשְׁכּוֹן' — the Mishkan is the language of mashkon (pledge/collateral). The Midrash (Shemot Rabba 31) explicitly equates the two words as sharing an essential meaning: the Mishkan is a divine pledge to Israel that the Shechina will dwell among them even if they sin. The word לְשׁוֹן is the standard Talmudic/Midrashic bechina marker ('language of X' = shares the essential nature of X). מַשְׁכּוֹן belongs in Package 1 as the semantic/etymology layer of the same drawing-force reality: a pledge (mashkon) draws the pledgor back; the Mishkan draws divine presence. The same root מ-שׁ-כ underlies both words, and Rebbe Nachman exploits this identity as a bechina statement.
additions.source_quote: שֶׁהַמִּשְׁכָּן הוּא לְשׁוֹן מַשְׁכּוֹן, שֶׁהוּא מַשְׁכּוֹן לְיִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁתִּשְׁרֶה שְׁכִינָה אֶצְלָם אֲפִלּוּ אִם יֶחֶטְאוּ

additions.reason: Line 18 of the source text states: 'זֶה בְּחִינַת רֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ' — 'this is the bechina of Rosh Chodesh,' specifically Rosh Chodesh Nissan which is Rosh Hashana for kings. The Rebbe explains that the erection of the Mishkan on Rosh Chodesh Nissan draws honor/leadership to all the heads/kings of the world, and זֶה בְּחִינַת introduces the conceptual equivalence: the renewal of the month IS a bechina of the renewal of leadership, which IS a bechina of the Mishkan's drawing force. Rosh Chodesh Nissan belongs in Package 1 as the calendrical expression of the same drawing-force reality — the moment when the tzaddik's Mishkan-power is actualized across all levels of leadership in the world.
additions.source_quote: וְעַל־כֵּן הָיָה הֲקָמַת הַמִּשְׁכָּן בְּרֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ נִיסָן דַּוְקָא, כִּי זֶה בְּחִינַת רֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ, שֶׁעַל־יְדֵי־זֶה נִתְחַדְּשִׁים כָּל הָרָאשִׁים כַּנַּ"ל

eitza_reclassification_review.reasoning: The node2_text explicitly includes the word בְּחִינַת ('הֵם בִּבְחִינַת עָפָר... בְּחִינַת מִשְׁכָּן'), which superficially looks like a bechina statement. However, the edge captures the causal direction: people who diminish themselves THEREBY become like dust, which has the Mishkan-quality. The self-diminishment is the CAUSE; acquiring the dust/Mishkan-nature is the EFFECT. The Rebbe's phrasing 'עַל־יְדֵי־זֶה הֵם בִּבְחִינַת עָפָר' (through this they are a bechina of dust) is an eitza construction — through X you become Y. The concept ממעיטין is not inherently the same nature as משכן; it is the path that leads to acquiring that nature. Correct classification: eitza.
Same logic as Edge 1980. The self-minimization produces the dust-quality (via the same passage), not shares its essence by definition. Eitza is correct.

concepts_examined_and_excluded.reason: Line 6 says 'כָּל הַצַּדִּיקִים הֵם רַק עֲנָפִים מִמֶּנּוּ' — all other tzaddikim are branches from the singular Tzaddik. This uses metaphor (ענף) to describe a relationship, not a bechina declaration. No בְּחִינַת or הַיְנוּ precedes עָנָף. The branch metaphor is a relational description, not a parallel-nature equation. Excluded.

Line 7 cites 'וְעַפְרוֹת זָהָב' as a verse in which all blessing/divine influence is drawn from the dust-quality. This is a proof-text for an existing bechina (עפר = drawing force), not a new bechina node. The gold-dust phrase names the phenomenon of השפעות flowing from עפר but does not establish a separate bechina-concept. Excluded.

concepts_examined_and_excluded.concept: אנשי ענתות / עניים שאינם מהוגנים (unworthy poor)
concepts_examined_and_excluded.reason: Line 8 introduces those who are NOT a bechina of עפר — giving charity to them is not like sowing on earth. This is a negative contrast case (people lacking the dust-quality), not a bechina-positive concept. It provides content for the evil mirror but the text does not use בְּחִינַת to equate them with any concept positively. Excluded from additions.

Lines 2-3 and 9-10 extensively discuss כח המכריח — the force that pushes things away from earth (and people away from the tzaddik). However, the text never uses בְּחִינַת language to equate כח המכריח with another concept. It is described causally (it separates people from the tzaddik) but not given bechina-identity. All four edges where כח המכריח appears in the dataset (edges 814, 1423, 1980, 2415) are correctly typed as eitza. Excluded from bechina additions.

Line 10 says that as one draws closer to the tzaddik one has more חשק (desire/longing), because of the drawing force. This is a causal observation, not a bechina declaration. No הַיְנוּ or בְּחִינַת precedes חשק. Excluded.
